titleEn: Ernest Shackleton turned a major disappointment in the Antarctic into fame back in Britain
titleZh: 沙克尔顿如何把南极的重大失意，变成在英国的名望
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Ernest Shackleton is one of the most well-known polar explorers in history. He’s mostly remembered for his incredible leadership following the sinking of his ship Endurance in the Weddell Sea in November 1915, which saved his life and the 27 others on board.
paragraphs.zh: 欧内斯特·沙克尔顿是历史上最著名的极地探险家之一。1915年11月，他的船“耐力号”在威德尔海沉没，救了他和船上其他27人的命。

paragraphs.en: Yet had you known Shackleton in 1895, his future fame as an Antarctic explorer would have seemed highly unlikely. At the time, he was an unknown officer in the merchant navy, and Antarctica meant little to him. He had never even put on a pair of skis.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，如果你在1895年就认识沙克尔顿，那么他作为南极探险家的未来名声似乎是极不可能的。当时，他是商船队的一名默默无闻的军官，南极对他来说意义不大。他甚至从未穿过一副滑雪板。

paragraphs.en: So how did Shackleton become such a famous polar explorer? This is one of the questions at the heart of my book The Grip of the Ice and the answer is suprising: his fame had as much to do with what he did back home as it did with his time on the ice.
paragraphs.zh: 那么，沙克尔顿是如何成为如此著名的极地探险家的呢？这是我的书《冰之握》（The Grip of the Ice）的核心问题之一，答案令人惊讶：他的成名与他在冰上的时间和他在家乡的所作所为有着同样大的关系。

paragraphs.en: Shackleton’s polar career started with the British National Antarctic Expedition, usually known as the Discovery Expedition (named after its ship). The venture was jointly organised by the Royal Geographical Society and the Royal Society and partly funded by the government. The gregarious Shackleton found a place on the expedition by befriending Cedric Longstaff, the son of one of the expedition’s major donors. On the March 15 1901, Shackleton was ordered to report to the Discovery’s commander, Robert Falcon Scott, at the expedition’s office in Mayfair. He would be the ship’s third lieutenant.
paragraphs.zh: 沙克尔顿的极地生涯始于英国国家南极探险队，通常被称为发现探险队（以其船命名）。这次探险由皇家地理学会和皇家学会联合组织，政府提供部分资金。合群的沙克尔顿通过与塞德里克·朗斯塔夫交朋友，在探险队中找到了一席之地，沙克尔顿是探险队一位主要捐赠者的儿子。1901年3月15日，沙克尔顿被命令到位于梅菲尔的探险队办公室向发现号指挥官罗伯特·福尔肯·斯科特报告。他将成为发现号的第三中尉。

paragraphs.en: Arriving in Antarctica in January 1902, they explored the continent’s coast and then spent the winter on board their ship in McMurdo Sound. During the months of polar darkness, conditions were too harsh for further exploration. Shackleton became a vital and well-liked member of the Discovery expedition. To help keep up morale while cooped up on board the ship, he edited The South Polar Times – the first magazine ever published in Antarctica.
paragraphs.zh: 1902年1月，他们到达南极洲，探索了大陆的海岸，然后在麦克默多湾的船上度过了冬天。在极地黑暗的几个月里，条件太恶劣，无法继续探索。沙克尔顿成为了发现号探险队的重要成员，也很受欢迎。为了在船上保持士气，他编辑了《南极时报》--第一本在南极洲出版的杂志。

paragraphs.en: Shackleton soon heard exciting news: Scott had selected him, along with the expedition’s zoologist and junior medic Edward Wilson, to accompany him on a journey towards the South Pole. This would be the expedition’s first major journey.
paragraphs.zh: 沙克尔顿很快就听到了一个令人振奋的消息：斯科特选择了他，沿着探险队的动物学家兼初级军医爱德华·威尔逊，一起前往南极，这将是探险队的第一次重大旅程。

paragraphs.en: Leaving the ship on November 2 1902, the journey started off well, with Siberian huskies helping to pull the men’s sledges. They were soon further south than any explorers before them. But things gradually began to unravel. The dogs weakened due to problems with their food, the men grew hungry on insufficient supplies and they couldn’t move their sledges forward all st once, drastically reducing their daily distances.
paragraphs.zh: 1902年11月2日，他们离开了这艘船，旅程开始得很顺利，西伯利亚哈士奇帮他们拉雪橇。他们很快就比之前的任何探险家都更往南了。但事情逐渐开始变得混乱。狗因为食物问题而虚弱，男人们因为补给不足而变得饥饿，他们无法立即移动雪橇，大大缩短了他们每天的距离。

paragraphs.en: Shackleton and Scott may also have had an argument on this journey, with Albert Armitage, the expedition’s second in command, later suggesting in his letters that Scott called Shackleton a “bloody fool” during a heated argument. Even so, they patched things up and trudged southwards. Eventually, they managed to lighten their sledges by leaving supplies for the return march in a depot, improving their rate of progress. However, their dogs continued to weaken so Shackleton and Wilson killed the sickest animals and fed them to the stronger ones.
paragraphs.zh: 沙克尔顿和斯科特在这次旅行中可能也发生了争执，探险队的副指挥阿尔伯特·阿米蒂奇后来在信中暗示，斯科特在一次激烈的争论中称沙克尔顿为“该死的傻瓜”。尽管如此，他们还是修补了事情，向南跋涉。最终，他们设法减轻了雪橇的重量，在一个仓库里留下了回程的补给品，提高了他们的进度。然而，他们的狗继续虚弱，所以沙克尔顿和威尔逊杀死了病得最重的动物，把它们喂给了强壮的动物。

paragraphs.en: By Christmas 1902, the men were also in trouble. Wilson inspected the men’s gums and noticed signs of scurvy – a disease we now know is caused by a lack of vitamin C. Soon, they were forced to turn back, having achieved a new furthest south record of around 480 miles from the South Pole on December 31 1902.
paragraphs.zh: 到了1902年的圣诞节，这些人也遇到了麻烦。威尔逊检查了这些人的牙龈，发现了坏血病的迹象--我们现在知道这种疾病是由缺乏维生素C引起的。很快，他们被迫返回，在1902年12月31日，他们创造了一项新的最远南方纪录，距离南极约480英里。

paragraphs.en: On the march back to the ship, Shackleton’s health deteriorated rapidly. As well as suffering from scurvy, he was also coughing up blood. When the last of their dogs was killed, Scott and Wilson pulled the sledge while Shackleton made painful progress on skis.
paragraphs.zh: 在返回船上的途中，沙克尔顿的健康状况迅速恶化。除了患有坏血病，他还咳血。当他们的最后一只狗被杀死时，斯科特和威尔逊拉着雪橇，而沙克尔顿则在滑雪板上痛苦地前进。

paragraphs.en: Eventually, on February 3 1903, they got back to the ship to find that the Morning, a relief vessel, had arrived.
paragraphs.zh: 最终，在1903年2月3日，他们回到船上，发现一艘救援船“早晨”号已经到达。

paragraphs.en: The Discovery was still trapped in the ice and, with winter closing in, Scott ordered that Shackleton return to New Zealand when the Morning sailed northwards on March 2 1903. Among polar historians, Scott’s decision has been controversial. Some suggest that Scott saw Shackleton as a potential rival, though there isn’t a great deal of evidence for this.
paragraphs.zh: 1903年3月2日，随着冬季的临近，斯科特命令沙克尔顿返回新西兰。在极地历史学家中，斯科特的决定引起了争议。一些人认为斯科特将沙克尔顿视为潜在的竞争对手，尽管没有太多证据证明这一点。

paragraphs.en: Early return and celebrity
paragraphs.zh: 早期回归和名人

paragraphs.en: So, Shackleton’s career as a polar explorer seemed to have got off to a bad start. While Scott sent him back with a glowing reference, he had been pronounced unfit for further Antarctic exploration. Frustratingly, he seemed “practically well” according to Gerald S Doorly, then a junior officer on the Morning, by the time he arrived in New Zealand and was in even better shape when he reached London.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，沙克尔顿的极地探险生涯似乎有了一个糟糕的开端。虽然斯科特给他写了一封热情洋溢的推荐信，但他被宣布不适合进一步的南极探险。令人沮丧的是，据杰拉尔德·S·多利（Gerald S Doorly）说，当他到达新西兰时，他似乎“实际上很好”，当他到达伦敦时，他的状态甚至更好。

paragraphs.en: Shackleton’s diaries show that he felt a mix of emotions: frustration, embarrassment and disappointment. He had been desperate to stay another winter and see the expedition through to its finish.
paragraphs.zh: 沙克尔顿的日记显示，他当时心情复杂：沮丧、尴尬和失望。他不顾一切地想再呆一个冬天，直到探险结束。

paragraphs.en: Yet studying this period, what amazed me was how Shackleton took advantage of his early return to Britain.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，研究这一时期，让我惊讶的是沙克尔顿如何利用他早期返回英国的机会。

paragraphs.en: As the only officer back from Antarctica, he was in a unique position to tell the public and the media what had happened on their journey. He wrote articles for The Illustrated London News and Pearson’s Magazine and gave lectures to enthralled audiences, eager to hear about his amazing journey towards the South Pole.
paragraphs.zh: 作为唯一一位从南极洲返回的官员，他处于一个独特的位置，可以向公众和媒体讲述他们旅程中发生的事情。他为《插图伦敦新闻》和《皮尔逊杂志》撰写文章，并为着迷的观众举办讲座，渴望听到他前往南极的奇妙旅程。

paragraphs.en: Shackleton was also involved in equipping a relief vessel, the Dundee whaler Terra Nova, to help free the explorers from the ice the following year. By early 1904, he’d even managed to land a job as secretary of the Royal Scottish Geographical Society.
paragraphs.zh: 沙克尔顿还参与装备了一艘救援船，邓迪捕鲸船泰拉诺瓦，以帮助探险家们在第二年摆脱冰层。到1904年初，他甚至设法找到了一份工作，担任皇家苏格兰地理学会的秘书。

paragraphs.en: The Discovery expedition transformed Shackleton from an unknown officer in the Merchant Navy into one of the best-known polar explorers in Britain. He’d also built a wealth of logistical experience and connections that left him perfectly placed to launch an expedition of his own – which he did in 1907, much to Scott’s annoyance.
paragraphs.zh: “发现号”探险使沙克尔顿从商船队一名默默无闻的军官变成了英国最著名的极地探险家之一。他还积累了丰富的后勤经验和人脉，这让他完全有能力发起自己的探险--他在1907年就这样做了，这让斯科特很恼火。

paragraphs.en: In his return to London, Shackleton had demonstrated his unique ability to make the very best of a disaster.
paragraphs.zh: 回到伦敦后，沙克尔顿展示了他在灾难中最大限度地利用机会的独特能力。
